children: Average scores for the July 2026 national bar exam and declining outcomes among the first three states to report test results suggest that lower pass rates will be the norm this year for the attorney licensing exam.

The national average score on July’s 200-question Multistate Bar Exam fell 1.7 points to 140.7 — the first decline since 2022, according to the National Conference of Bar Examiners, which designs the attorney licensing exam. The dip comes on the heels of a 12-year high posted by July 2025 bar takers, and brings the average MBE score more in line with recent years, the data show.
The average MBE score is a key national metric that provides an early indication of how many law graduates will pass the exam required by most states to practice law.
Meanwhile, Arkansas, West Virginia and Wisconsin each posted a pass rate decline of 5 percentage points or more. They are the only states thus far to release pass rates.

The National Conference did not offer a reason for the MBE score decline on Tuesday, but said the introduction of the NextGen UBE, the new national bar exam, was not the cause as those scores were not included in the newly released figures. Ten jurisdictions administered the NextGen exam in July with that national average score expected in October.

Notre Dame law professor Derek Muller, who tracks bar exam trends, said the decline is likely to fuel speculation that over-reliance on AI for studying and an increase in student accommodations in law school were factors.

Students who use AI shortcuts in law school may not be gaining the foundational knowledge they need to pass the bar, Muller said, though he cautioned that it's too early to tell. He also said law schools tend to be more generous with accommodations — such as extra time on tests — than bar examiners, meaning test takers who are accustomed to those accommodations might struggle to perform under the time pressure of the bar exam.
Here's more from the bar examiners' report:
July's 1.7-point decline is the largest year-over-year change in the average MBE score since 2018, with the exception of the 2020 exam that was disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic.
Approximately 76% of July test takers were taking the bar for the first time, down slightly from 77% the previous year.
In July, 44,472 people took the MBE, about 5% fewer than the previous year. That decline was largely due to 10 jurisdictions administering the new bar exam.
